claim: The β-hemoglobinopathies, such as sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia, are one of the most common genetic diseases worldwide.
source: The β-hemoglobinopathies, such as sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia, are one of the most common genetic diseases worldwide and are caused by mutations affecting the structure or production of β-globin subunits in adult hemoglobin.

claim: The β-hemoglobinopathies are caused by mutations affecting the structure or production of β-globin subunits in adult hemoglobin.
source: The β-hemoglobinopathies, such as sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia, are one of the most common genetic diseases worldwide and are caused by mutations affecting the structure or production of β-globin subunits in adult hemoglobin.

claim: δ-globin has high homology to β-globin.
source: δ-globin, the subunit of adult hemoglobin A2, has high homology to β-globin and is already pan-cellularly expressed at low levels in adult red blood cells.

claim: δ-globin is pan-cellularly expressed at low levels in adult red blood cells.

claim: Insertion of a KLF1 site alone is insufficient to upregulate δ-globin.

claim: Multiple transcription factor elements are necessary for robust upregulation of δ-globin from the endogenous locus.
source: Instead, multiple transcription factor elements are necessary for robust upregulation of δ-globin from the endogenous locus.
